title: Join-as-you-go
subtitle: Connecting motifs during the last round so no seaming is needed
excerpt: Join-as-you-go (JAYG) connects each new motif to its neighbours during the final round — replacing a separate seaming step with a join worked into the edge of the adjacent piece. The result is a neat, flat join with no finishing seams.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book — motif joining methods. Standard modern British crochet finishing technique.

glossaryTerms.definition: Abbreviation for join-as-you-go. A technique for joining crochet motifs during the last round of each new motif, by working a slip stitch or chain-slip-stitch into the corresponding chain space of the adjacent finished motif.
The chain space on a finished motif into which a JAYG join is worked. On a granny square this is typically the corner ch-2 space or the side chain-1 space between clusters.

heroPrompt: Two granny squares in cream and dusty blue DK cotton side by side on a pale surface, with their shared edge joined flat by a JAYG chain-slip-stitch join — the neat central line of the join visible between them.

content.text: The standard way to finish a granny-square blanket is to complete all the squares, then seam them together.

. The motifs are joined as they are made.

On the final round of the new square, wherever a chain space falls against an edge of an adjacent finished square: work half the chain, then insert the hook into the corresponding chain space of the finished square and work a slip stitch, then complete the remaining chain. Example, replacing a ch-2 corner space: ch 1, sl st into corner ch-2 space of adjacent square, ch 1 (the two ch-1 halves stand in for the ch-2).

Before starting, lay all the finished squares (those that will be complete before the JAYG row begins) on a flat surface in the correct layout. Work row by row: the first row of squares is completed normally. From the second row onward, each new square joins to one or more finished neighbours as it is made. Corner-to-corner joins need a three-way join at the meeting of four squares — work a sl st into the existing corner join rather than the chain space of any single square.
When JAYG is not the right choice
When you want a raised decorative seam on the right side (use slip-stitch seam instead).
When the motifs are irregular shapes where the join positions vary per motif (seaming after is more flexible).
When the blanket layout may change mid-project — JAYG is committed, seaming after is adjustable.
